source.title: Group Whitening: Balancing Learning Efficiency and Representational Capacity
source.authors: Lei Huang; Yi Zhou; Li Liu; Fan Zhu; Ling Shao

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests random-label training accuracy under normalization settings, including CNNs on CIFAR-10, using a different method and measures from the claim’s cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports random-label fitting accuracy for a linear classifier and MLPs on MNIST and CNNs on CIFAR-10. The MLP results are described in text and shown in Figure 5; CNN results are shown in Figures A4–A5. Exact CNN values cannot be assigned from the supplied figure text. Other normalization results, including ImageNet and COCO benchmark accuracy, do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Appendix E measures CIFAR-10 CNN training accuracy after SGD, bearing on V1 through the same basic training-and-fitting measure. Relative accuracies do not establish near-zero training error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the constraint experiments. The authors also conclude that their proposed group whitening improves visual-recognition performance and that constraint analysis helps explain normalization's dependence on batch size and group number.
record.recipe_differences: Studies random-label fitting under normalization choices, rather than directly testing the broad gradient-training claim or comparing the cited training recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Training accuracy changes with normalization type, group number, batch size and network depth.

fits_no_version.finding: GN/GW reduce random-label fitting accuracy for MNIST linear and shallow MLP models; moderate normalization can improve fitting in the deeper MLP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization imposes representation constraints whose effects on random-label fitting depend on group number and model architecture.

record.peer_reviewed: Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), as identified in the supplied text’s references and paper context; venue field states Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
record.problems: The random-label fitting results are primarily figure-based; exact values for the reported accuracy differences are unavailable in the supplied text. The text does not state initialization details or directly report whether training error reached zero or near zero.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results omitted. Normalization performance on ImageNet, COCO and machine translation does not test the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Absolute zero or near-zero CNN training error; sufficiently large CNNs; stated random initialization; explicit corrupted/random CIFAR labels; CIFAR-100; width scaling and early stopping.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and extra student neurons.
Absolute training-error degradation with depth and prevention by identity shortcuts. Increasing normalization gains relative to Base does not establish either.
Initialization comparisons, signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature evolution and recovery or divergence.
Accuracy trajectories or time to accuracy for BN versus no normalization, higher-learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is justified by the recorded relative accuracies: absolute fitting performance and the sufficiently-large-model condition are unresolved. Restrictive normalization causing lower accuracy also does not contradict V1's explicit allowance for regularized recipes. Appendix E does not explicitly identify its CIFAR-10 labels as random.

versions.untested_parts: The text tests random-label fitting under normalization choices, but does not state whether the models were trained from random initialization, whether training classification error reached zero or near zero, or whether CIFAR-100 was tested. The CNN figure reports training-accuracy differences rather than exact accuracy values.

rows.subject: linear classifier
rows.operation_detail: Fit random labels on MNIST for 1,000 epochs using SGD; report the best training accuracy among the stated learning rates.
rows.value: GN and GW have lower training accuracy than the model without normalization; exact values figure only
rows.note: Text explicitly says normalization lowers training accuracy in this random-label fitting setup; exact points are not recoverable from the supplied figure text.
rows.check: A linear classifier on MNIST is outside V1's convolutional-network and CIFAR scope. Lower accuracy than Base does not establish the claimed effect.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: random-label fitting with normalization on MNIST and CIFAR-10
reader_labels.reason: Training accuracy depends on normalization and its settings; the paper reports lower accuracy for normalized linear and one-layer models, and degradation at large group numbers or small batch sizes (R1–R5). These results do not establish whether sufficiently large randomly initialized models reach near-zero error.
